paragraphs: Rabbi Chanan son of Pitum, a tanna, is mentioned in Taanit 22b. Hyman also refers to Levi bar Pitum in Yuchasin and directs the reader to his entry.

notes.text: The heading has Pitus, פיטוס; the notices have Pitum, פיטום, and an earlier machine heading also read Pitum. The final-letter difference remains a source-glyph question.

The saved named Davidson Taanit 22b paragraph explicitly names Chanan ben Pitum, a student reporting Rabbi Akiva. This supports the body’s Pitum without deciding frozen heading Pitus or the older machine heading’s final letter. The separate Yuchasin/Levi bar Pitum cross-reference remains Hyman’s report; no source repair or identity binding is made.

Hyman’s printed notice (vol. III, p. 1010) is headed פיטום, Pitum, where the supplied text has פיטוס, Pitus. The consulted Taanit 22b names Rabbi Chanan ben Pitum, a student who reports in Rabbi Akiva’s name. The reference to Levi bar Pitum in Yuchasin is Hyman’s report, and the exact Yuchasin passage remains unverified.
